title: Avatar Medical and Kyber Awarded €3.7 Million to Widen Access to Immersive 3D Imaging in Hospitals

html:
Avatar Medical and Kyber today announced they have been awarded up to €3.7 million through the French government’s France 2030 program to develop Avatar MediVerse, a project designed to make immersive patient-specific 3D medical imaging available wherever clinicians and patients need it.

Today, showing a patient or clinician anatomy in true, glasses-free 3D requires significant computing power located alongside the display, which can limit access to specially equipped rooms. MediVerse is designed to shift that computing power to a remote location and stream the immersive 3D experience in real time. A surgeon could show a patient the tumor they are preparing to remove during a consultation, access the same patient-specific anatomy while planning the procedure, and bring that view into the operating room.

Avatar MediVerse combines two complementary French technologies. Avatar Medical brings Avatar Medical Vision, its FDA-cleared and CE-marked software that converts standard CT and MRI scans into interactive, lifelike 3D visualizations without requiring manual segmentation, along with experience working with more than 20 hospitals across the U.S. and Europe. Kyber provides the ultra-low-latency real-time infrastructure that remotely renders and streams the experience.

Unlike streaming a conventional flat video, delivering true depth requires sending a separate image to each eye in real time, fast enough for the anatomy to respond immediately as a clinician moves or rotates it for better viewing.

“Interacting with medical imaging in real time is one of the hardest latency problems there is.” said Jean-Baptiste Kempf, CEO of Kyber. “A delay that would be invisible in a video call breaks the image entirely when each eye is receiving its own view. Solving it is what makes the rest possible. By combining Avatar Medical’s immersive visualization with Kyber’s real-time streaming infrastructure, MediVerse is designed to make those interactions seamless across locations and devices. It is a strong example of how French deep-tech innovation can address a meaningful, real-world healthcare challenge.”

For Avatar Medical, MediVerse is an important step in its broader vision of Visual Intelligence for Surgery, making patient-specific visual information available throughout the surgical care journey rather than tying advanced visualization to a single workstation or room. By separating the computing power from where the images are viewed, MediVerse could make interactive 3D visualization more scalable across hospitals, health systems and geographically distributed care environments.

“We chose to build this with the best real-time technology available, and it happens to be French,” said Elodie Litzler, deputy CEO and co-founder of Avatar Medical. “Neither of us could do this alone. What we are after is not simply new equipment in hospitals, but a change in how patients and clinicians understand what they are looking at, and where that understanding can take place.”

Built on open-source technologies, the project also aims to give hospitals greater control over their infrastructure and reduce their dependence on proprietary remote visualization platforms.

The award was granted through France 2030’s “Innovative Technologies for Immersive Virtual Worlds” call for projects following evaluation by an independent expert committee, with Bpifrance overseeing implementation on behalf of the French government.

About Kyber

Kyber is a French deep tech company that develops real-time infrastructure for healthcare, robotics, cloud rendering and AI-driven video applications. Learn more at https://kyber.tech .

About Avatar Medical

Founded in 2020, Avatar Medical is pioneering Visual Intelligence for Surgery, building a scalable solution that transforms medical imaging into actionable visual information throughout the surgical care journey. Its flagship solution, Avatar Medical Vision, converts CT and MRI scans into interactive, lifelike 3D visualizations instantly and without segmentation, giving clinicians a more intuitive way to understand patient-specific anatomy, plan procedures, collaborate and communicate with patients. From consultation and preoperative planning through the operating room, the company is working to make visual intelligence accessible wherever critical surgical decisions are made. Originating from research conducted at Institut Curie and Institut Pasteur, Avatar Medical has FDA-cleared and CE-marked technology products. It works with more than 20 hospitals across the U.S. and Europe. Learn more at avatarmedical.ai .
